messages:
Sarah (AE): FYI Acme's POC is failing when they send their long prompt bundle — they see a 413. Can SE help?
Mia (SE): Thanks, digging in. Do we have the raw request size and any proxy logs from their side?
Alex (Acme): Here's what we saw client-side:  POST /v1/generate  payload ~ 6.7MB, server returned 413 Request Entity Too Large.
Alex (Acme): Their UI concatenates ~25 documents + system prompt, ~45k characters, then base64-encodes attachments.
Mia (SE): Ok two things to consider: (1) API gateway/nginx limit (413) vs (2) model context token limit (model_max_tokens). Both can manifest as truncation or errors. Which model are you hitting?
Alex (Acme): We're hitting rwd-32k-001. We expect model supports 32k tokens but our payload hits the edge when counting embeddings + base64 attachments.
Diego (Infra): DeployBot shows nginx upstream responded 413 at the gateway for that IP at 1763356901. Looks like default client_max_body_size 4M on their LB.
Mia (SE): Two immediate workarounds: (A) send payload with Content-Encoding: gzip to reduce bytes over the wire, or (B) chunk the context—stream messages or upload large context to a signed blob store and pass a context_url ref.
Mia (SE): Example curl with gzip:
```bash
cat body.json | gzip -c -9 | curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  --data-binary @-
```
Alex (Acme): Nice. If we gzip, will the API accept and decompress automatically?
Mia (SE): Yes our gateway supports Content-Encoding: gzip and will decompress. But note any upstream proxy between client and us must preserve the header and support streaming.
Diego (Infra): For POC we can also bump the LB client_max_body_size to 10M for Acme's IP for the week. I created an internal ticket.
Alex (Acme): That would help short-term. Concern: when we tried truncation earlier the assistant answers lost context unpredictably. Is there a recommended pattern to avoid semantic loss?
Mia (SE): Two patterns we recommend: (1) Offload long docs to embeddings + retrieval—store docs in vector DB and only send retrieved chunks in prompt. (2) If you must send whole context, chunk by semantic boundary and stream chunks; keep a short summary slot in the prompt header.
Diego (Infra): Also confirm model token limits: rwd-32k-001 enforces model+prompt<=32k tokens. We apply a server-side check and will return a 400 if model limit exceeded; 413 means transport size. Different errors.
Alex (Acme): Got it. We also base64 attachments which inflate size ~33%. We'll try gzip + chunking first.
Mia (SE): I'll send a reference snippet for client-side chunking and an optimization: instead of base64 inline, upload binary to S3 and include a short pointer in the prompt. That cuts payload a lot.
Mia (SE): Quick chunking pseudo:
```js
// 1) split docs into <8KB chunks
// 2) POST each chunk to /v1/context?upload=true -> returns context_id
// 3) call /v1/generate with context_ids array + system prompt
```
Alex (Acme): Sounds good. What's the impact on pricing / tokens if we do retrieval vs full inline?
Mia (SE): Retrieval costs token usage only for the retrieved text you include in the final request, plus any storage/ingest costs if you use our optional object store. For Dedicated customers we can advise on batch pricing for high-volume retrieval.
Sarah (AE): Diego, can we expedite the LB increase for the POC IP so they can test gzip without hitting 413?
Diego (Infra): Yep — temporary LB rule created, will be live in 10m. Monitoring via DeployBot.
DeployBot: LB rule applied for IP 198.51.100.23, TTL 7 days.
Alex (Acme): Tried gzip + same request, now 200 and response looks complete. Thanks all.
Mia (SE): Great — follow-up actions: (1) Alex to implement S3 pointers for attachments, (2) try retrieval/embedding flow for doc corpus, (3) we'll monitor any model limit 400s and advise truncation or model variant.
Sarah (AE): I'll update the deal notes and pricing options (Dedicated reserved cap if they need consistently big contexts).
Alex (Acme): thanks everyone :thumbsup:
